info.title: Submission API
info.description:
The Submission API handles inbound form submissions from external sources such as epilot Journey frontends, embedded forms, and third-party integrations.

When a customer completes a Journey, the resulting data is sent to this API. The API creates one or more epilot entities (e.g. contacts, opportunities, orders) from the submitted payload, attaches uploaded files, and records opt-in consent choices.

**Key concepts**

- **Submission entity** – A structured record created in epilot from the data captured in a Journey step.
- **Source** – Identifies where the submission originated (`source_type` + `source_id`), e.g. a Journey ID.
- **Nonce** – A single-use token that prevents duplicate submissions. Use `getNonce` to check whether a nonce was already consumed before re-submitting.
- **Opt-ins** – Consent records (e.g. email marketing permission) captured alongside the submission.

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description:
Operations for creating Journey submissions and checking submission nonces.

A submission is the primary unit of data ingress from epilot Journeys. Each submission can create multiple epilot entities and attach files via S3 references from the File API.

post.description:
Creates a submission from a public-facing Journey or other external source.

**Access:**
- Public Journeys and non-journey sources accept anonymous requests or public Journey tokens (by design). A token bound to a Journey (`journey_id` claim) may only submit to that Journey (`source_id`).
- Private Journeys require a user or portal-user token (public Journey tokens are rejected). Tokens of the Journey's owner organization are accepted; tokens of other organizations (e.g. sharing partners) must be able to access the Journey via journey-api (`entity:view` on the shared journey).
- Journey submissions always land in the Journey's owner organization.

The API processes the payload, creates the specified entities in epilot, resolves file attachments from the File API S3 references, and records any opt-in consent entries.

**Idempotency:** Use the `journey_submit_id` field as a client-side idempotency key to avoid duplicate submissions on retries
(enforced when idempotency is enabled for the organization).

200.description:
The same `journey_submit_id` was already accepted for this organization. No second
submission was created. `submission_id` is present once the first submission's entity exists.

201.description: Submission accepted; entities are created asynchronously. The body is currently empty.

submission_id.description: The ID of the created submission entity

503.description:
Another request with the same `journey_submit_id` is still starting the submission. Retry
after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`; the retry answers 200 `duplicate: true` once
the first request started, or creates the submission if the first request never did.

get.description:
Check whether a submission nonce has already been consumed (i.e. exists in storage).

Nonces are single-use tokens attached to Journey submissions to prevent duplicate processing. Before re-submitting, clients can call this endpoint to verify whether a previous submission with the same nonce was already recorded.

This endpoint is public (no authorization), so it only answers whether the nonce was used. It does not return the submission or organization the nonce belongs to.

parameters.description: The nonce token to look up

NonceNotFound.summary: Nonce has not been used yet

EpilotAuth.description: Epilot Authorization Bearer Token - public access token / user token

BadRequestResponse.description: Bad request - invalid or missing parameters

example.message: entities must contain at least 1 item

UnauthorizedResponse.description: Unauthorized - missing or invalid authentication credentials

ForbiddenResponse.description: Forbidden - caller does not have permission to perform this action

example.message: Insufficient permissions to create submissions for this organization

NotFoundResponse.description: Not found - the requested resource does not exist

submission_id.description: Id of the submission entity created by the first request, when already known.

JourneyContextOffline.description:
Set by the journey app when the submission was recorded offline and replayed later.
The known keys are typed; unknown keys are accepted (newer app versions may add more).

submission_id.description: ID of the submission that consumed this nonce

organization_id.description: The organization ID associated with this nonce

ttl.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the nonce expires

exists.description: Whether the nonce has already been consumed

nonce.description: The nonce token (only set when it exists)

SubmissionPayload.description: Holds content and meta information for a Journey submission

organization_id.description: Target organization ID – defaults to the token's organization when omitted

journey_submit_id.description:
Client-generated idempotency key (uuid v4), one per submission attempt. When idempotency is
enabled for the organization, a repeated POST with the same id returns 200 `duplicate: true`
instead of creating a second submission (503 with `Retry-After` while the first request is
still starting).

source_type.description: Type of source that generated the submission (e.g. `journey`, `frontend`)

source_id.description: Identifier for the source, e.g. the Journey ID or frontend component ID

opt_ins.description: Opt-in consent records to create alongside this submission (e.g. email marketing consent)

entities.description: One or more epilot entities to create from this submission. Must contain at least one entry.

_ivy_opportunity_ids.description: Related Ivy Opportunity IDs (deprecated – do not use for new integrations)

SubmissionEntity.description: An epilot entity to create as part of the submission

_schema.description: The entity schema type. Must be `submission` for standard Journey submissions.

description.description: Human-readable description of the submission, used as the entity title

journey_context.description:
Runtime context the journey app attaches to the entity. Documented keys are listed below;
any other key is accepted and stored as sent.

journey_revision_id.description: The journey revision the submission was produced with (usually a string; any value is accepted).

files.description:
Files to attach to the Submission entity as relations. Each file must be an S3 reference
previously obtained from the epilot File API upload flow.

filename.description: Override the file name displayed in epilot

_tags.description: Tags to apply to the created File entity

relation_tags.description: Relation labels for the file attachment (e.g. `signed_document`)

example.request: I would like to know more about home EV charging options

OptIn.description: A consent opt-in record captured during the submission

identifier.description: The identifier for the consent record (typically the customer's email address)

meta.description: Additional metadata about the opt-in (e.g. source, timestamp)

S3Reference.description: An S3 object reference returned by the epilot File API after a successful upload
